# AMC Frecency Launcher

<!-- Generated by tools/build-templates.mjs from template.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**List Template** for Universal Theme · direction: living · APEX 23.1+ · v1.0.0

A launcher that learns: it counts which destinations this user opens and how recently, and at the next page load lifts the top three into ranked Your most used tiles with a heat meter and the last time they were opened, while the rest keep the developer's order in a compact grid.

**Use it for:** Home pages and workspace launchpads with 6 to 20 destinations, where different users live in different corners of the app: finance opens Invoices and Month-end close, sales opens Orders and Customers.

## Install

- **APEX 23.1 to 25.x (or any version, through the Builder):** App Builder > your app > Shared Components >
  Export/Import > Import `dist/legacy/amc_tpl_frecency_launcher.sql` (Component Export). It creates the
  template in Universal Theme and its Static Application File(s) in `amc-templates/`.
- **APEX 26.1+ (APEXlang):** copy `dist/apexlang/shared-components/themes/universal-theme/list-templates/amc-frecency-launcher.apx` and
  `dist/apexlang/shared-components/static-files/amc-templates/` into the app, add the entries from
  `dist/apexlang/static-files.snippet.apx` to `shared-components/static-files.apx`, then run the apexlang gates.

## Use

Create or pick a List (Shared Components > Lists), add a **List** region and set **Appearance > List Template** to **AMC Frecency Launcher**. In APEXlang: `componentAppearance { listTemplate: @amc-frecency-launcher }`.

Launcher list template that adapts to each user. Every time the user opens an entry, the time is stored in this browser's localStorage under amc-tpl-frecency-launcher:<application id>:<list id> (time stamps per entry, at most 30 per entry, entries unused for 120 days are forgotten; nothing is sent to the server). At page load each entry gets a frecency score, the sum of 0.5 to the power of age divided by a half-life of 10 days over its opens, and entries opened at least twice are ranked: the top 3 move into a numbered Your most used list, the rest stay in the developer's order as a compact grid. The order only changes at page load, never under the pointer. List items are moved in the DOM, so Tab order and screen-reader order always match the screen; the new favourites are announced politely once when they change. A first-time user sees the developer's order as full tiles with a hint. Reset order clears what was learned for this list. Attribute 1 is a description, Attribute 2 a badge such as 14 overdue, Attribute 3 an optional learning key: set it when the entry link carries values that change, otherwise the link without session, checksum and clear-cache values is the key. Template options: Adapt quickly uses a half-life of 3 days, Four favourites ranks 4, Filled favourites paints the ranked tiles in the primary color, Discreet hides the heat meter and last-opened time for shared screens, Rows shows everything else as a divided list. Without JavaScript, or when storage is blocked, it is a plain grid of launch tiles. Reduced motion removes the hover lift, the meter fill and the arrival glow. English UI strings to translate in the template: the two hint sentences, Reset order, Your most used, Everything else, and the data-announce, data-reset-done and data-opened attributes on the wrapper; relative times come from Intl.RelativeTimeFormat in the page language.

## List entry attributes

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| A01 | Description |
| A02 | Badge |
| A03 | Learning key |

## Template options

| Option | Class | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Adapt quickly | `amc-TFrecencyLauncher--fast` | Uses a half-life of 3 days instead of 10, so the favourites follow this week's work, for example during a month-end close. |
| Four favourites | `amc-TFrecencyLauncher--four` | Ranks the top 4 instead of 3, shown in one row in regions wider than about 700 pixels. |
| Filled favourites | `amc-TFrecencyLauncher--filled` | Paints the ranked tiles with a primary-colored gradient so the personal part of the page stands out. |
| Discreet | `amc-TFrecencyLauncher--discreet` | Hides the heat meter and the last-opened time, for shared screens and kiosks; the ranking still applies. |
| Rows | `amc-TFrecencyLauncher--rows` | Shows the entries that are not ranked as a divided list instead of a grid, for side columns. |
